input: Fix the squeaky third stair on the staircase

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The fix could range from a quick surface-level remedy (lubricant, screws from above) to a full structural repair involving dismantling the tread or riser — the intended depth of the fix changes everything.
Whether the staircase is interior or exterior, and what it is made of (wood, carpet-covered, laminate) directly determines which repair method is viable.
Knowing whether this is a DIY fix or a job for a hired professional determines how technical and detailed the plan needs to be.
Access to the underside of the stair (e.g. open basement below vs. closed soffit) is a hard physical constraint that rules in or out entire categories of repair techniques.
The tools and materials already on hand (screws, wood glue, lubricant, drill) determine whether a hardware run is needed before starting.
The standard for 'done well' could be total silence, a significant reduction in noise, or a cosmetically invisible repair — this sets the bar for which solution is acceptable.
Some fixes (face-screwing, for example) leave visible marks, while others are hidden. Knowing the priority between speed/ease and appearance guides the method chosen.

gold.taskTitle: Fix the squeaky third stair on the staircase
gold.taskDescription: Diagnose and repair the squeak on the third stair of a staircase to eliminate the noise when stepped on.

questions.title: How deep a fix are you aiming for?
questions.description: Is the goal a quick patch (e.g. lubricant or a couple of screws) or a thorough structural repair that fully addresses the root cause of the squeak?

questions.title: What material and type is the staircase?
questions.description: For example: solid hardwood, plywood treads, carpet-covered, laminate overlay, interior vs. exterior — the material dictates which repair methods are viable.

questions.title: Will you do this yourself or hire someone?
questions.description: Clarifies whether the plan should be a step-by-step DIY guide or advice on what to brief a tradesperson.

questions.title: Can you access the underside of the stair?
questions.description: Is there an open space (e.g. basement or open-back stairs) beneath the third step, or is the soffit fully enclosed? This is a hard constraint on repair technique.

questions.title: What tools and materials do you already have?
questions.description: Knowing what is on hand — drill, screws, wood glue, construction adhesive, lubricant — determines whether a hardware store trip is needed before starting.

questions.title: What counts as a successful repair to you?
questions.description: Is the goal complete silence under all foot traffic, a noticeable reduction in squeaking, or simply quieter on light steps? Sets the acceptance bar for the fix.

questions.title: How important is keeping the repair invisible?
questions.description: Some fixes (face screws, for instance) leave visible marks on the tread. Should the repair be cosmetically hidden, or is speed and simplicity the priority?
